item.title: UPDATED: Sweden's new rules will make citizenship harder for children
item.description: A government bill tabled this week would tighten Sweden’s citizenship rules by requiring children to apply in their own right, rather than by notification. Older minors will need to demonstrate good conduct and knowledge of the Swedish language and society.

item.title: Swedish government tells Migration Agency 'limited need' for work permit exemptions
item.description: Sweden's government has asked the Migration Agency to start from the premise that "the need for exemptions is limited" when drawing up its list of professions that should be excused the new higher salary threshold for a work permit when it comes into force in June.

item.title: 'Building Ikea furniture': The best things about dating a Swede
item.description: We asked The Local's readers to tell us what their favourite things about dating a Swede are, and here are some of their responses.

item.title: Why high-skilled workers feel betrayed by Sweden
item.description: In this week's podcast: anger over retroactive citizenship requirements, Prime Minister speaks out on teen deportations, and salary limit exemptions for work permit holders.

item.title: 'You arrived before things got insane': Moving to Sweden is tougher now
item.description: The Local’s Nordic Editor Richard Orange reflects on how easy it was for him to come to Sweden and then get citizenship ten years ago, and contrasts that with the gruelling process faced by his colleagues, before running through the week's news.

item.title: Europe, UK seek closer ties a decade after Brexit
item.description: Ten years after the referendum that led to Brexit, Britain and the European Union must close ranks in an increasingly unstable world, their leaders said on Saturday.

item.title: European debate over nuclear weapons gains pace
item.description: European leaders, worried about threats from a nuclear-armed Russia and doubts about the future of US security commitments, are increasingly debating whether to bolster nuclear arsenals on the continent.

item.title: UPDATED: Your questions about Sweden's new citizenship law
item.description: Sweden's government announced more details of its new citizenship law on February 9th, which left our readers with a lot of questions. We've tried to find some answers.

item.title: KEY POINTS: Should foreign workers in Sweden join a union?
item.description: For many international workers in Sweden, joining a trade union might not be something that crosses your mind, especially if it's not common in your home country. Here are the benefits and key things to bear in mind when considering joining.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Migration minister proposes letting teenagers finish studies before deportation, 8-month-old baby to be deported alone to Iran, and other news from Sweden on Monday.
